repository.name: jobFynder-BE-nestJS
repository.description: This is for BE rewamp to nestJS from nodeJS

commits.message:
feat(network): add work-event-derived relationship engine

Auto-connection network module: relationships form only from real work
events (submission created/interview/placed, assignment created, mutual
message exchange) via a single logRelationshipEvent() writer and an
append-only event log. No manual connect-request/accept-decline flow.

Wires triggers into existing bench submission/assignment services and
messenger send(), points User directly (no duplicate person/company
tables) reusing UserDetails for job title/company/location.

feat(network): full spec build-out — strength scoring, mute fix, endpoints

Fixes a real bug: mute was writing to the shared relationship row
(NetworkRelationship.status), which meant if A muted B, B's view of A
was affected too. Mute is now purely per-viewer via
NetworkRelationshipMute, matching spec 2.5's explicit rule.

Extends the schema with origin, strengthLabel, and interaction/
submission/placement counts. Adds the nightly strength-scoring batch
job (event points x age-decay, Strong/Active/Quiet labels with a
dormancy override) instead of the old naive incremental score. Adds
manual-connect, directory search, job-context matches, and network
settings endpoints. Adds a /skills file documenting the ordered-pair
rule, the both-parties-replied rule, and where scoring weights live.

docs: add full implementation spec set (NRM, identity, employment, etc.)

Master build plan + 9 numbered specs + invariants file for the next
phased implementation. Full copy also placed in jobFynder-FE-vite so
either repo's sessions have complete context without switching repos.

docs: add Hermes architecture freeze + developer guide

Companions to the NRM/identity/employment spec set already in docs/ —
the architecture doc is the frozen source of truth for how Hermes
integrates with Core, and the developer guide is the per-page endpoint
reference for building against it.
docs: add CLAUDE.md pointing every session to jobfynder-invariants.md

extend User model for unclaimed contacts (NRM Part 3)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs: add reconciliation decisions file

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: use DROP INDEX not DROP CONSTRAINT for users_email_key/users_slug_key

users_email_key and users_slug_key were created via plain CREATE UNIQUE
INDEX in 20251218184137_create_user_table and 20260626120000_add_user_slug,
not as named table constraints, so ALTER TABLE ... DROP CONSTRAINT failed
on a fresh database with "constraint does not exist".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add employer/employment/seat schema and resolveAccountMode()

Reuses Organization as `employer` (Decision 3) rather than duplicating
the tenant record; EmployerAssociation and OrgTeamMember are left
untouched since they conflate employment with paid access, which is
exactly what the seat/employment split exists to avoid. New Employment
and Seat models carry the consent-gated activatedAt boundary the spec
requires. resolveAccountMode() takes an explicit timestamp (never
defaults to now) and treats concurrent active seats across employers as
ambiguous, returning hybrid with all ids null rather than guessing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add relationship provenance columns and Company table (NRM Part 2/6)

Stamps ownership on NetworkRelationship at creation only, via
resolveAccountMode(actorUserId, occurredAt), per invariant 9. Adds
createdByUserId/employerContextId/ownership/employmentId to
NetworkRelationship and actorEmploymentId/employerContextId to
NetworkRelationshipEvent (docs/03-employment-visibility-spec.md Part 6).
Builds the Company reference table fresh (docs/01-nrm-comprehensive-spec.md
Part 2.3) — distinct from Organization and the untouched legacy
VendorCompany. logRelationshipEvent() now takes an explicit actorUserId
instead of relying on the userAId-is-actor convention; all five call sites
updated accordingly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add identity_merge_audit table, snapshot writer, and resolvePerson()

Per docs/02-identity-resolution-spec.md Parts 5 and 7.2. Builds only
the audit trail and the merge-chain resolver — no claim or merge logic
yet, per docs/10-reconciliation-decisions.md Decision 1 (person == User).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add admin unmerge procedure for identity merge audit (spec Part 6)

Replays identity_merge_audit.preMergeSnapshot in reverse inside one
transaction: restores the source person and its relationship(s),
including the surviving relationship's pre-merge counters when a
merge combine happened, repoints original events by ID, and leaves
post-merge events untouched while reporting their count (spec 6.3).
Guards against re-running on a non-COMPLETED audit row.

Adds NetworkEventType.MERGE_REVERSED for a direct, audit-only marker
event insert that bypasses logRelationshipEvent()'s counter/timestamp
side effects. Admin-only controller gated by crm_admin role.

Record Decision 4: snapshot writer must cover UserDetails before merge ships

captureSide() only snapshots the User row, but several Part 4 field
reconciliation rules (headline, location, isSearchable,
availabilityIsPublic) govern UserDetails columns instead. Harmless
today since merge isn't built yet, but whoever builds it next must
either extend the snapshot writer to cover UserDetails first, or
restrict reconciliation to columns that actually live on User.

Build identity resolution merge algorithm (spec Parts 3-4, signup claim)

Implements the merge engine as a complete, callable, independently
tested unit: IdentityMergeService.mergeUnclaimedRecord() (Part 3.1-3.3,
one transaction, snapshot-first, atomic source retirement, ordered-pair
renormalization via a new NetworkRelationshipService.repointRelationship
ForMerge(), combine handling with event dedup, MERGE marker event, creator
nudge) and claimMatchingRecordsForSignup() (Part 3.4, exact verified-email
matching capped at 50 with the rest reported as queued). Field
reconciliation (Part 4) lives in a pure, separately tested function.

Closes the Decision 4 gap by extending captureSide()/captureSnapshot()
and IdentityUnmergeService to cover UserDetails, so the UserDetails-backed
fields Part 4 can touch (location, isSearchable, availabilityIsPublic)
are reversible. Adds Decision 5: is_external is derived from isClaimed
at query time, never stored.

Not wired into any real signup or email-verification flow yet — that
connection point is a separate, dedicated session.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Resolve availability_status mapping, add Decision 6 for missing headline column

Confirmed by direct schema search (not memory): availability_status maps
to UserDetails.currentAvailabilityId (FK into the CurrentAvailability
lookup table) — its Part 4 rule is "claimed wins, always," a no-op, now
named explicitly in reconcileFields() instead of listed as excluded.
Added a test proving the source's currentAvailabilityId is discarded
even when the target's is empty, matching the no-op fields rather than
the adopt-if-empty ones.

headline has no column anywhere in the schema under any name (About is a
documented, unrelated bio field) — added Decision 6 stating Part 4
reconciliation for it stays incomplete, and merge won't touch it, until
a real column exists.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Wire identity merge engine into email verification (spec Part 1.1, 3.4)

Calls claimMatchingRecordsForSignup() from AuthService.verifyEmail()
right after isEmailVerified is set — the only place in the codebase
that flips this flag, and it fires exactly once since the token is
nulled on use. Merge failures are caught and logged with the user id,
never allowed to block the person's own signup/verification.

Add one-off seed script for a test unclaimed contact

Lets us manually exercise claimMatchingRecordsForSignup() against a
real local database without wiring up any of the deferred merge
sources (Decision 2).

Add local signup/email-verification test script

Lets claimMatchingRecordsForSignup() be exercised end to end without
the frontend or a real email inbox, since registerUser() never sends
a verification email and resendVerificationEmail() requires real SMTP.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix email/verify-email crash chain found via signup/verify test script

1. mergeUnclaimedRecord() flipped a source contact's isClaimed to true
   without clearing its email/slug, colliding with the target it was
   being merged into under users_email_claimed_key /
   users_slug_claimed_key (partial unique, WHERE isClaimed = true) —
   since claim candidates are matched by that exact email in the first
   place, this failed on every signup-claim merge. IdentityUnmergeService
   already restores email from the pre-merge snapshot on reversal, which
   is the tell that merge was supposed to clear it going in.

2. AuthService.verifyEmail() ran the user through transformUser() twice:
   once inside usersService.update(), then again on its own AuthUser
   result. The second pass read `.id` off an object that only has `_id`,
   silently producing `_id: undefined` and crashing
   AuthSessionService.establish() downstream with a Prisma
   "userId: undefined" error. Pre-existing since the initial commit,
   unrelated to the identity-merge work — just never exercised
   end-to-end until now.

Added a regression test for each, verified against the pre-fix code to
confirm they actually catch these bugs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Wire logProfileView() into ProfileService; test the mutual-exchange rule

Profile views were computing the anti-noise rule correctly in
logProfileView() but nothing ever called it - getProfileDetailsByViewer()
had no path to the Network module. Wired it in fire-and-forget (a profile
view is a weak background signal, not worth delaying a real page load for),
guarded against self-views and anonymous viewers, with a .catch() safety
net since the existence-check query isn't self-guarded the way
logRelationshipEvent() is.

Also adds direct unit tests for maybeLogMutualExchange() covering both
anti-noise branches (one-way conversation logs nothing; a real reply logs
MESSAGE_EXCHANGE_MUTUAL exactly once), which previously had only a stubbed
mock with no assertions.

Records Decision 7 in the reconciliation doc: six spec triggers
(application, interview scheduled/completed, offer extended, resume share,
referral, service request/completed) have no underlying feature to wire to
yet, so a future session doesn't guess at mapping them onto whatever module
looks closest.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Close unclaimed-person profile leak and harden directory search access control

GET /profile/details/:identifier had no isClaimed check at all, so any
caller (including anonymous) who knew or guessed an unclaimed person's
UUID could view their full profile. Fix scopes visibility to the
person's createdByUserId, per NRM spec Part 12 / invariant 20, and
returns the same NotFoundError a nonexistent id would produce so the
response can't be used to confirm the record exists.

Also adds an explicit isClaimed: true filter to directorySearch() as
defense in depth — unclaimed persons were only excluded incidentally
by lacking a UserDetails row, not by any guaranteed check.

Adds network-relationship.service.spec.ts and profile.service.spec.ts
covering all six Part 12 access-control rules with a negative case
for each (the network module previously had zero tests).

Add narrow crm_admin exception to unclaimed-profile visibility

getProfileDetailsByViewer() denies unclaimed-profile access to everyone
except the creator (commit e2860c7). Adds one deliberate, scoped
exception: a crm_admin viewer may also view an unclaimed profile, for
operational reasons like spotting stale unclaimed contacts. Every use
is logged for audit. No other role gets the exception, and no other
access rule (directory search, private notes, relationship lists) is
touched.

Documented as Decision 8 in docs/10-reconciliation-decisions.md so a
future session doesn't mistake this for a regression against
invariant 20.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add task schema and owner-scoped CRUD (Activity module, spec Part 6)

Builds the task table with grouping fields (groupedRecordIds,
groupedRecordType, ruleKey) plus snoozedUntil, and owner-scoped CRUD:
create, list (with derived-state filters computed at query time, never
persisted or batch-computed), get, update, complete, dismiss, snooze.

Auto-generation rules, the Activity embed, and the Next Actions view
are out of scope this session (Part 7 build order steps 2-5).

Adds Decision 9 to the reconciliation doc: NetworkNudge is a narrow
predecessor to this table and is left untouched, migration deferred to
its own session.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add Activity embed API (spec Part 6.3)

GET /activity?record_type=&record_id= returns { timeline, actions,
can_create_action } for any record type. Timeline is pluggable via a
TimelineSource interface; only NetworkRelationshipTimelineSource exists
today (record_type=relationship, backed by NetworkRelationshipEvent).
Any other record_type gracefully degrades to an empty timeline instead
of erroring, since no general "module events" concept exists in the
schema yet. Actions reuse Task.relatedType/relatedId, which already
work uniformly across record types. can_create_action is a static true
pending a real permission model.

Records the schema gap as Decision 10 in
docs/10-reconciliation-decisions.md so a future session extending the
embed to submission/job doesn't re-derive this investigation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Build the three Activity auto-generation rules (spec Part 4)

interview_prep and offer_deadline fire synchronously from
BenchSubmissionService.updateSubmissionStatus() when a recruiter records
interviewScheduledAt/offerDeadline; no_response_chase runs nightly and
groups by vendorRelationship, never per submission (invariant 23).

Adds an admin-editable RuleConfig table for the per-rule cap/threshold/
lead-time tunables, a deliberate narrow override of "config, not
database" — crm_admin-only, bounded, audited, seeded with the spec's
defaults (Decision 11). TaskService.complete() now fans a completed
grouped chase task's submissions out to lastChasedAt so a resolved
group isn't regenerated the next scan.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(resume): guard the resume CRUD routes and add a JSON create endpoint

Found while wiring the resume builder to real persistence (it currently
saves to localStorage only, never calling this module): list/get/update/
delete on /resume all read req.user (set by JwtAuthGuard), but none of
the five relevant routes had the guard applied anywhere -- class,
method, or otherwise. Every one of them would throw on req.user._id for
any real caller. Never caught because the frontend has never called
these routes yet.

Fixed per-method rather than at class level -- parse-resume
intentionally tolerates a guest caller (parses and returns data without
persisting when there's no logged-in user), and generate-section /
fields don't touch req.user at all, so those three stay open. Added
resume.controller.spec.ts asserting the guard is present on the five
that need it and absent on the three that shouldn't have it, so this
doesn't regress silently again.

Also added the one real gap in the existing CRUD surface: POST /resume
only existed as a file-upload-then-parse flow (parse-resume). There was
no way to create a resume from typed-in JSON, which is what the
resume-builder's manual-entry and LinkedIn-import flows need. Added
POST / with a validated CreateResumeDto (the existing PUT/:id keeps its
untyped body -- it's also handling multipart file uploads, and forcing
strict array/object validation there risks breaking whatever's already
working for that combined path).

Schema: added Resume.builderMetadata (nullable JSONB, additive
migration, no impact on existing rows) to hold resume-builder fields
with no dedicated column -- location, links, work authorization,
market preferences, skill categories. Kept as one flexible bucket
rather than five new fixed columns since the builder's shape is still
evolving.

Verified: `nest build` and `tsc --noEmit` clean, `npx prisma generate`
picks up the new field with no schema errors, resume.controller.spec.ts
passes (6/6). Not yet verified against a live database -- this is a
schema migration and needs `prisma migrate deploy` run against the
real Postgres instance, which isn't something to do without the
person who owns that database in the loop.

feat(resume): add resume variants (label, variantType, parentResumeId)

Second piece of the resume-persistence foundation, on top of this
same PR's auth-guard fix. A "variant" (role-based, job-specific,
company-specific, recruiter-requested, or blind-resume) is just
another `resumes` row -- same content, tagged with a parent and a
type -- not a new table or subsystem.

Schema: additive migration adding `label`, `variantType`, and
`parentResumeId` (self-relation, ON DELETE SET NULL so deleting a
base resume doesn't cascade-delete every variant built from it).
`label` is new because there was no way to give a resume record its
own display name before ("Java Tech Lead - Fintech Focus" as opposed
to `title`, which is the professional headline printed on the resume
itself, e.g. "Senior Java Developer" -- those are different things
and would otherwise collide once a user has more than one resume).

New endpoints, both ownership-checked the same way every other route
here is (only works on a resume the caller already owns):
- POST /resume/:id/variants -- copies :id's content into a new row,
  tagged with parentResumeId=:id, the given label/variantType, and an
  optional targetRole/targetCompany merged into builderMetadata.
- GET /resume/:id/variants -- lists variants of :id.

Extended resume.controller.spec.ts to cover both new routes (8/8
passing). `nest build` / `tsc --noEmit` clean, `prisma generate` picks
up the new fields with no errors. Same caveat as the first commit:
not yet run against a live database.

feat(bench): add GET /bench/submissions/mine (consultant reads own submission history)

Third piece of the resume-persistence foundation work, unrelated to
the Resume table itself but needed for the same reason: the consultant
Performance view had zero real backend anywhere and was about to get
a brand-new tracking system invented for it. Checked first -- the
`Submission` table (job title, client, status, dates, resumeVersionId)
already tracks exactly what that view needs. It just had no read path
for the consultant *behind* the assignment, only for the recruiter who
filed it (every existing /bench/submissions/* route is
`@Roles('bench_sales')` and scoped by `submittedByRecruiterId`).

Added `BenchSubmissionService.listMySubmissions()` and
`GET /bench/submissions/mine`, deliberately without `@Roles` (unlike
every other route in this controller) -- it's not recruiter tooling,
so any authenticated role can call it, scoped by
`consultantAssignment.consultantId` instead. Read-only: no new way for
a consultant to write or change a Submission's status, since that has
real commission/placement implications and should stay
recruiter-controlled.

Added bench.controller.spec.ts asserting the existing recruiter-only
routes keep their `@Roles('bench_sales')` guard and that
`submissions/mine` deliberately doesn't have one -- 2/2 passing. `tsc
--noEmit` clean.

feat(billing): add multi-tenant subscription/billing module (Stripe-first)

Full first pass at the requested Subscription module: Customer, Plan/
PlanPrice, Subscription, Invoice/InvoiceLineItem, Payment, Coupon,
PaymentMethod, WebhookEvent, and SubscriptionEvent audit trail
(prisma/schema.prisma + migration 20260822020000). Customer binds to
either an Organization or a standalone User (never both) so both
org-level and individual-consultant subscriptions are supported without
forcing solo users into creating an org.

Stripe is fully wired end-to-end (customer/subscription/invoice/payment
creation, webhook ingestion with signature verification + idempotency,
daily dunning retries via the existing ScheduleModule cron). Razorpay
gets the identical PaymentGatewayAdapter interface but every method
throws NotImplementedError -- an explicit, loud stub rather than fake
logic, per the agreed Stripe-first rollout.

Reused existing infrastructure instead of reinventing it:
- org-access/ (CASL-based RBAC) for multi-tenancy -- no new OrgPermission
  codes needed, since employer:billing_manage_subscription /
  employer:billing_view_invoices (and the sp: equivalents) were already
  seeded in org-defaults.ts and unused until now.
- ScheduleModule (already registered in app.module.ts) for the dunning
  cron, matching cron/expire-invitations.service.ts's pattern.
- The three-layer config pattern (env.validation.ts Joi schema ->
  configuration.ts typed block with isConfigured getter -> ConfigService)
  for STRIPE_*/RAZORPAY_* env vars, so the app still boots without
  billing configured.
- MailService.sendEmail for dunning notices, apiResponse/pagination.util
  for controller responses, the resume-intelligence.controller.spec.ts
  guard-reflection pattern for the new spec tests.

Proration is a pure, fully unit-tested ProrationService (upgrade/
downgrade/same-day/zero-length-period cases) -- no gateway calls, so the
math is independently verifiable. Upgrades default to immediate
proration+invoice; downgrades default to taking effect at period end
(both overridable via ChangePlanDto.prorationBehavior), matching Stripe's
own default behavior.

One non-obvious fix: main.ts disables Nest's body parser and wires
json()/urlencoded() manually, which would otherwise consume the webhook
request body before Stripe's signature check can see the raw bytes --
added express.raw() scoped to /api/billing/webhooks ahead of the JSON
parser. Also had to add @CsrfExempt() to both webhook controllers, since
the global CsrfGuard (APP_GUARD) requires a browser Origin/CSRF-cookie
pair that a server-to-server Stripe webhook will never send -- caught by
tracing the guard chain, not by testing against live Stripe traffic
(no credentials in this environment).

Explicitly not built this pass (flagged in the plan, not silently
skipped): Razorpay implementation, tax calculation, multi-currency
conversion, and a billing portal/checkout UI.

Verified: tsc --noEmit clean, `nest build` clean, full existing jest
suite (127 tests across 23 suites) still passes, plus 27 new tests
(8 ProrationService unit tests, guard/permission-metadata reflection
tests for every new controller). Not verified against a live Stripe/
Razorpay account or a live database -- no credentials or DB connection
in this environment, same caveat as every other backend change this
session.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(credits): add credit ledger, top-up purchases, and gate Resume Builder AI actions

Builds on the Subscription module: CreditGrant (a "lot" of credits with its
own source and expiry) + CreditTransaction (append-only audit trail) +
TopupPack/TopupPurchase (one-off credit-pack purchases via Stripe
PaymentIntents). Balance is always computed live as the sum of non-expired
grants' remaining amounts -- no cached balance field to keep in sync, so
there's no separate "reconcile the balance" bug class to worry about.

Credit sources implemented, all three requested:
- Plan-included, refilled each period: Plan.features.includedCredits
  (already in the Subscription schema, previously unused) is granted via
  SubscriptionService.create() for the first period and
  SubscriptionService.syncFromGateway() for renewals -- both call the same
  idempotent CreditService.grantPlanIncludedCreditsForPeriod(), which checks
  for an existing PLAN_INCLUDED grant created within the current period
  before granting again.
- One-off top-up packs: admin-managed catalog (TopupPack), purchased via a
  new PaymentGatewayAdapter.createOneOffPayment() method (Stripe
  PaymentIntents -- the existing adapter only had subscription-oriented
  methods). Fulfillment happens off the existing payment_intent.succeeded/
  payment_intent.payment_failed webhook handlers, extended to also check
  TopupPurchase (a Payment row lookup alone would miss these, since one-off
  top-ups don't have an Invoice).
- Manual admin grants: POST /billing/credits/customers/:customerId/grant,
  crm_admin only -- also how refunds work when a paid AI call fails after
  credits were already debited.

Expiry (per the "expire at end of billing period" decision): every grant
carries its own expiresAt. Consumption is FIFO by soonest-expiring lot
first (credit-lot-selection.ts, extracted as a pure function specifically
so the ordering/spillover/tie-breaking logic is unit-testable without a
database). A daily cron (CreditExpiryService) zeroes out expired lots'
`remaining` and logs an EXPIRE transaction for reporting -- not required
for balance correctness (getBalance/consume already filter by expiresAt)
but keeps CreditGrant-level numbers and the audit trail honest.

Wired into the first real consumer, per the "Resume Builder AI actions"
decision: tailor, quality/analyze (ATS check), summary/suggest, bullets/
suggest, skills/suggest, and match in resume-intelligence.controller.ts
are now credit-gated -- debited before calling Hermes, refunded if Hermes
fails, hard-reject with InsufficientCreditsError (402) if the balance is
too low. `parse` (resume import/onboarding), `feedback/analyze`, and
`submissions/evaluate` stay free -- the latter two are recruiter/bench-
sales tooling, not consultant AI spend. Per the "blocked until they
subscribe" decision, a user with no Customer record (never subscribed)
gets the same 402 rather than a free allotment.

Costs per action (src/billing/credits/credit-costs.config.ts) are
placeholder numbers -- no product pricing was specified for this pass,
called out explicitly rather than silently invented as if authoritative.

Verified: tsc --noEmit clean, `nest build` clean, full jest suite (143
tests / 26 suites, up from 127/23) passes -- including 8 new pure-function
tests for the FIFO lot-selection logic and guard/permission-metadata tests
for the two new controllers. Not verified against a live Stripe account or
database, same caveat as the rest of this billing work.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(collaboration): resume sharing via link + threaded comments

New module, independent of the billing PRs (#4/#5) -- based on main, no
Subscription/Credits dependency, since sharing/feedback isn't a paid
feature.

ResumeShare (a token-scoped, revocable, optionally-expiring link with
VIEW or COMMENT permission) + ResumeComment (threaded via
parentCommentId, OPEN/RESOLVED status, author is either a platform User
or an anonymous name+email pair for external viewers).

Per the "anyone with a share link" decision: PublicShareController
carries no JwtAuthGuard and no other guard -- the 24-random-byte token
(crypto.randomBytes, same primitive org-invitation.service.ts already
uses for invite tokens, just wider) is the entire access control for
GET .../shared/:token, GET .../shared/:token/comments, and POST
.../shared/:token/comments. Added a deliberate negative test
(public-share.controller.spec.ts) asserting no guard metadata is present
at the class or handler level, specifically so a future edit that
accidentally adds JwtAuthGuard here breaks CI immediately instead of
quietly locking out every logged-out viewer.

Owner-side routes (CollaborationController, JwtAuthGuard) create/list/
revoke share links, list all comments across every share for triage, and
resolve threads -- ownership checked the same way resume.controller.ts
already does it (findFirst({id, userId}), 404 either way so a non-owner
can't distinguish "not found" from "not yours").

Comment posting works both ways: an anonymous viewer through a
COMMENT-permission share link (CreatePublicCommentDto -- authorName
required, authorUserId left null), or the owner themselves replying to
feedback (CreateOwnerCommentDto, authorUserId/authorName from the JWT).
Both paths validate a given parentCommentId actually belongs to the same
resume before threading a reply under it.

Deliberately not built: rich-text/highlight-range anchoring for
quotedText (stored as plain text, no document-position tracking), email
notifications when a comment is posted, and any UI -- backend only, same
as the rest of this session's work.

Verified: tsc --noEmit clean, `nest build` clean, full jest suite (110
tests / 20 suites on this main-based branch) passes, plus 10 new tests
(ShareService token-validation branch coverage, guard-presence checks for
both controllers -- including the negative "no guard" test above). Not
verified against a live database, same caveat as the billing PRs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(hermes-drafts): review queue for Hermes email-parsed drafts

HERMES-850 (Hermes repo) parses hotlist/requirement emails into draft
objects in Hermes's OWN storage -- publishing a draft there only flips a
status flag inside Hermes, it never creates anything in Core. Nothing in
this codebase previously read those drafts at all. This is the other
half: a human review queue that turns an approved draft_job_requirement
into a real JobPosting.

New module src/hermes-drafts/, mounted at /hermes-drafts, gated to
bench_sales + crm_admin (JwtAuthGuard + RolesGuard):
- GET /hermes-drafts, GET /hermes-drafts/:id -- proxy Hermes's own
  /drafts endpoints (4 new methods added to the existing HermesClient in
  src/hermes/hermes.client.ts: listDrafts/getDraft/publishDraft/
  rejectDraft, same send() transport every other Hermes call already
  uses). Getting one draft also returns a best-effort "suggestedJob" for
  draft_job_requirement drafts, built by HermesDraftsService.
  suggestJobFromDraft() from Hermes's parsed record
  (payload.structured_data.email_parsing.records[n]) -- deliberately
  never fabricates employmentTypes/workAuthorizations when Hermes didn't
  actually extract a value, since ApproveJobRequirementDraftDto requires
  at least one employment type and a made-up default would misrepresent
  what the source email said.
- POST /hermes-drafts/:id/approve-job -- takes the SAME body shape
  /jobs/from-parsed already validates (ApproveJobRequirementDraftDto
  extends the existing CreateParsedJobDto), reuses
  JobsService.createJobFromParsed() unchanged rather than writing new
  job-creation logic, then calls Hermes's publish endpoint to mark the
  draft consumed. The reviewer's submitted body is what's created --
  nothing from the unreviewed draft is trusted directly. Job lands in
  DRAFT status, same as any manually-created job; publishing it is still
  the existing Jobs module flow, not bypassed here.
- POST /hermes-drafts/:id/dismiss -- calls Hermes's new
  POST /drafts/:id/reject (added alongside this in the Hermes repo,
  mirroring publish).

Scope decision, made explicitly rather than defaulted into: only
draft_job_requirement creates a Core record this pass.
draft_hotlist has no single existing Core entity to map to.
draft_consultant_profile/draft_recruiter_profile/
draft_bench_sales_profile map conceptually to a User + UserDetails, but
auto-creating a real, potentially-authenticatable account from
unverified parsed email content is a product/security decision, not
something this service defaults into -- those draft types are listable
and dismissable through the same queue but don't auto-create anything.
draft_vendor_list/draft_channel_note are out of scope entirely.

Verified: tsc --noEmit clean, `nest build` clean, full existing jest
suite (110 tests / 19 suites, no regressions) plus 10 new tests --
guard/role reflection on the controller, and service-level coverage of
the suggestion mapping (including the two "must not fabricate a
required field" cases) and the approve/dismiss flows against a mocked
HermesClient/JobsService. No frontend for this queue exists yet. Not
verified against a live Hermes instance -- HermesClient's isConfigured
flag is false without real HERMES_API_TOKEN/HERMES_BASE_URL in this
environment, same caveat as every other Hermes-dependent change this
session.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(hermes): accept full parsed job payload on POST /hermes/job/create

Upgrades the Hermes-facing job-creation endpoint from a bare title/
client/location stub (zero real callers, verified) to the same
CreateParsedJobDto the human-triggered LinkedIn/Indeed URL-import flow
already uses (POST /jobs/from-parsed) -- skills, employment types, work
authorizations, benefits, rate range, description, and the external-
source/recruiter-contact fields all now resolve through the one
existing, validated JobsService.createJobFromParsed code path instead
of a second hand-rolled one.

Every job created this way is owned by a new fixed system account,
'Jobfynder Sourcing' (migration 20260829010000), not an ad hoc or
unclaimed-contact row -- unclaimed contacts are scoped to a single
creating user's private book and never appear in directory search
(invariant 20, skills/jobfynder-invariants.md), which is the wrong
visibility model for who owns a job-board posting. The real external
recruiter is captured via JobExternalSource/JobRecruiterInfo exactly as
the URL-import flow already does it. Adds JobSourceType.EMAIL alongside
the existing LINKEDIN/INDEED/CAREER_PAGE/OTHER values.

Every posting still lands as JobStatus.DRAFT -- this endpoint proposes,
nothing here publishes. Prerequisite for wiring Hermes's email-parsing
pipeline (claim-and-verify confirmed listings) to actually create job
board postings; the Hermes-side push itself is separate follow-up work.

Verified: tsc --noEmit clean across the whole project; eslint clean on
every changed line (pre-existing CRLF/prettier noise in this checkout
confirmed via git stash to predate this change, left untouched).
